title: Alternating groups and permutation parity
chapterTitle: 8. Solutions to the Chapter Review Questions
section: Chapter 6 Review Questions ▷ Question 8: a subgroup-order counterexample
terms: alternating group; even permutation; odd permutation; sign homomorphism; double transposition.

exposition.text:
The sign of a permutation is +1 if it can be written as an even number of transpositions and

question.text:
How many elements of A have no fixed points and have exactly two cycles in their disjoint-
6
cycle decomposition?
(A) 40 (B) 90 (C) 120 (D) 130 (E) 180

solution.text:
The only possible cycle types are (2, 4) and (3, 3). Both are even because their signs are
6−2 2
(−1) = 1. Type (2, 4) has 6!/(2 · 4) = 90 permutations, and type (3, 3) has 6!/(3 · 2!) = 40.
The total is 130.

question.text:
How many surjective group homomorphisms are there from A to the additive group Z/3Z?
4
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 4

solution.text:
Every element of order 2 must map to 0, because its image has order dividing both 2 and 3.
Thus every map kills the normal Klein four subgroup V = {e, (12)(34), (13)(24), (14)(23)}
and factors through A /V , a cyclic group of order 3. A map from this quotient is surjective
4
exactly when a generator maps to 1 or 2, giving two maps.

question.text:
What is the largest possible order of an element of A ?
7
(A) 7 (B) 6 (C) 10 (D) 12 (E) 5

solution.text:
A 7-cycle is even and has order seven. The partitions that could give larger orders in S are
7
5 + 2 (order ten) and 4 + 3 (order twelve), but each has odd sign. The other even cycle types
have order at most seven.
